chosen_line.card: All Streams Flow to the Sea

q1_what_did_you_play: I spent both energy on damage: All Streams Flow to the Sea into Nibbit for 9 (Charge already counted), then Water's Edge for 6, for 15 total. That leaves Nibbit at 19/42 and I eat the full 12, going to 36/70. The reasoning is the clock. Nibbit is a single enemy at 34 HP hitting for 12 a turn; at roughly 15 damage a turn I need three attacking turns to kill it, and the enemy only gets to swing on the first two of those. That is 24 incoming across the fight. Anything I spend on defense now does not shorten the fight, it just moves the same 34 HP further out and buys the enemy another swing to be paid for later. With 48 HP I can afford two hits comfortably, so the cheapest total-damage-taken plan is to spend everything on closing the gap. I put All Streams first purely because it is the bigger hit and I wanted it on the board before anything could change; the page gives me no reaction or ordering effect that makes the sequence matter.
q2_other_line_considered: Gyorin Formation alone, and I weighed it seriously — it is the closest call on the page. Two energy for 10 Block plus 6 at the start of next turn is 16 block against a 12-damage telegraph, which is more raw value than 15 damage and would have left me at 46/70 with a head start on the following swing. I rejected it because it deals zero: the fight still needs 34 damage out of me, and a turn of pure defense just adds a turn in which Nibbit gets to attack. Tallying both lines out to the kill, the totals came out within a few HP of each other, and I took the aggressive one because it ends the fight sooner and does not depend on future draws cooperating. I also looked at the middle line, Coral Guard plus All Streams — 5 Block and 9 damage, take 7 — and dismissed it as the worst of both: not enough block to matter against a 12, and it throws away a third of my damage.
q3_what_it_gave_up: It gave up all 16 points of blocking, including the 6 that would have carried into next turn, and it gave up the safe HP total: I am at 36 instead of 46, and after the next swing I will be at 24, which is where the fight starts to have a floor I care about. It also gave up flexibility — if my next hand is short on damage, the tempo I bought here is wasted and I will have taken 12 for nothing.
q4_different_intent: Yes. Attack for 12 against 48 HP is exactly the band where racing is affordable; move the number and the answer moves. A substantially bigger hit — say high teens or more — makes Gyorin Formation correct, because 10 Block plus 6 next turn converts a threatening swing into a survivable one and my HP stops being a resource I can freely spend. A defensive or buffing intent, or any turn where Nibbit was not attacking at all, would have made the all-damage line strictly free rather than a trade, and I would have played it with no deliberation. A telegraph of a multi-hit attack would also have changed it, since 10 Block absorbs a big single hit far better than several small ones and I would have had to re-weigh Coral Guard.
